title: Westerns
tagline: From Silverado to Once Upon a Time in the West without noticing the water got hot.

levels.name: Popcorn
levels.note: Ensemble fun, charm and a quick draw.

levels.name: The modern way in
levels.note: Recent Westerns that play like thrillers.

levels.name: Classic Hollywood
levels.note: Ford, Hawks, Mann, Wayne, Stewart and Cooper.

levels.name: Spaghetti
levels.note: Leone, Corbucci and Eastwood. Dirtier, meaner, louder.

levels.name: Revisionist
levels.note: The myth falls apart: Peckinpah, Unforgiven, Dead Man.

levels.name: Final boss
levels.note: The grimmest, the saddest and the slowest.

core.b: Four drifters, one corrupt town, and Kevin Kline, Kevin Costner, Danny Glover and Scott Glenn having a ball. The most fun a Western has ever been.

br.note: Mel Brooks tears the whole genre apart. Rude, and still very funny

br.t: Back to the Future Part III
br.note: Marty and Doc in 1885

core.t: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
core.b: Newman and Redford, charming outlaws on the run. 'Who are those guys?'

br.note: Redford alone in the Rockies, learning to survive

core.b: Kurt Russell's Wyatt Earp and Val Kilmer's Doc Holliday, who steals the film. 'I'm your huckleberry.'

br.note: Sam Raimi's quick-draw tournament: Sharon Stone, Gene Hackman, young DiCaprio and Crowe
The Brat Pack as Billy the Kid's gang

core.b: Seven Samurai moved to Mexico: Yul Brynner, Steve McQueen and that theme tune.

br.note: The original, on the Action and Asian action ladders
Lee Marvin and Burt Lancaster on a rescue mission into Mexico
Gary Cooper and Burt Lancaster's grinning villain in Mexico

core.b: The Coen brothers: a 14-year-old hires Jeff Bridges' drunk marshal to hunt her father's killer.

br.note: Christian Bale and Russell Crowe get a killer onto a prison train
The tighter, talkier original with Glenn Ford
John Wayne's Oscar-winning Rooster Cogburn

core.b: Tarantino's spaghetti tribute: a freed slave and a German bounty hunter go after his wife.

br.note: Tarantino traps eight liars in a cabin in a blizzard

core.w: Very bloody, and brutal scenes of slavery.

core.b: Kevin Costner and Robert Duvall as cattlemen pushed too far. Slow burn, then one of the best gunfights ever filmed.

br.note: Costner's three-hour epic with the Lakota

core.b: John Ford's coach full of misfits, and the shot that made John Wayne a star.
Howard Hawks: John Wayne drives cattle to Missouri and Montgomery Clift mutinies.

br.note: Gregory Peck's epic range war
Samuel Fuller: Barbara Stanwyck rules a county with 40 hired guns
Lurid Technicolor melodrama, from the Scorsese list

core.t: The Treasure of the Sierra Madre
core.b: Bogart and two prospectors strike gold in the Mexican mountains, and greed does the rest. 'Badges? We don't need no stinking badges!'
Hawks again: Wayne, Dean Martin and a kid hold a jail against a gang. Laid-back and lovely.

br.note: Hawks remakes Rio Bravo with Wayne and Robert Mitchum

core.b: Gary Cooper's marshal waits for the noon train and the killers on it, while the town abandons him. Told in real time.

br.note: A posse decides to hang three men. Grim and angry
Eastwood survives a lynching and comes back with a badge

core.b: A gunfighter tries to hang up his guns on a homestead. 'Shane! Come back!'

br.note: Eastwood remakes Shane as a ghost story

core.t: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
core.b: Ford, Wayne and James Stewart: who really killed the outlaw, and does it matter? 'Print the legend.'

br.note: Wayne's last film: a dying gunfighter's final week

core.b: James Stewart's bounty hunter drags Robert Ryan's killer across the Rockies and comes apart on the way. Anthony Mann at his darkest.

br.note: Stewart chases a stolen rifle and the brother who took it
Mann and Stewart's widescreen revenge
Stewart as a reformed raider guiding settlers

core.b: Budd Boetticher: Randolph Scott and a newlywed couple held hostage by outlaws. 78 minutes, not a wasted line.

br.note: Scott hunts the men who killed his wife
Scott, a bounty and a long ride

core.b: Wayne's darkest role: years hunting the Comanche who took his niece, and maybe planning to kill her.

br.note: Ford's cavalry in colour: Wayne's last patrol
Ford's cavalry: Henry Fonda's arrogant colonel
Ford's cavalry trilogy, part three: Wayne and Maureen O'Hara
Ford's poetic OK Corral, with Henry Fonda
Joan Crawford vs Mercedes McCambridge. Feverish and strange

core.w: Racist hero, deliberately, and dated depictions of Native Americans.

core.b: Eastwood and Lee Van Cleef as rival bounty hunters, and a pocket watch. The best of the Dollars films.

seq.note: Where it started: Yojimbo remade with Eastwood

core.t: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
core.b: Three men, a fortune in gold, a civil war, and the greatest stand-off ever filmed.

br.note: Leone's revolution film, also called A Fistful of Dynamite
Henry Fonda and Terence Hill: a comic farewell to the spaghetti Western

core.b: Sergio Corbucci: a man drags a coffin through the mud, and what's inside is a machine gun.

br.note: Lee Van Cleef hunts a man who might be innocent
Corbucci's comic revolution romp
Franco Nero, mud and mysticism: the last great spaghetti

core.b: Eastwood's farmer turns killer after his family is murdered, then collects a family of strays.

br.note: Eastwood's vengeful stranger paints a town red. Nasty
DiCaprio, the bear and a frozen crawl for revenge
br.warn: Very violent, including the bear attack.

br.note: Marlon Brando directs himself in a revenge Western

core.b: Peckinpah's ageing outlaws, one last job, and the bloodbath that changed screen violence.

br.note: Peckinpah's gentle elegy for two old lawmen

core.b: Peckinpah: James Coburn hunts his old friend Kris Kristofferson. Bob Dylan sings 'Knockin' on Heaven's Door'.
core.w: Watch the 2005 special edition, not the theatrical cut.

core.b: Eastwood's old killer takes one last job and finds there's nothing heroic about it.

br.note: John C. Reilly and Joaquin Phoenix as hitman brothers. Funny, then tender
Christian Bale escorts a dying Cheyenne chief home

core.t: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
core.b: Brad Pitt's Jesse and Casey Affleck's starstruck Robert Ford. Slow, gorgeous, haunting.

br.note: The Coens' six Western tales, from silly to devastating

core.b: Jim Jarmusch: Johnny Depp drifts west, a wanted man, guided by a Native American called Nobody. Black and white, Neil Young guitar.

br.note: Kelly Reichardt: settlers lost in the desert. Minimal and hypnotic
Michael Fassbender guides a lovesick Scottish boy west. Short and strange

core.b: Corbucci's snowbound bounty-hunter nightmare, with Klaus Kinski. The bleakest ending in Westerns.
The Coens' modern Western: a hunter finds drug money in the Texas desert, and Javier Bardem's killer comes for it. Tommy Lee Jones's old sheriff can't keep up.
core.w: Sudden, cold violence, and an ending that refuses to resolve.

br.note: Modern Texas bank robbers and Jeff Bridges as the ranger after them
The first modern Western: one-armed Spencer Tracy arrives in a desert town with a secret
Paul Newman's heel of a Texas rancher's son
John Sayles: a border sheriff digs up his dead father's legend

br.t: The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada
br.note: Tommy Lee Jones drags his friend's body to Mexico
A murder on a Wyoming reservation in the snow
Wolverine's last ride is really Shane with claws
Walter Hill: Nick Nolte's Texas Ranger vs his old friend's cartel

core.b: Robert Altman: Warren Beatty and Julie Christie build a brothel town in the snow. Leonard Cohen songs. Super depressing.

br.note: Peter Fonda's cult drifter Western: lovely and sad
Dustin Hoffman, 121 years old, tells his story
Burt Lancaster's scout tracks an Apache raiding party. Brutal and intelligent
Australia: an outlaw must choose between his brothers. Written by Nick Cave. Grim as anything
Kurt Russell's posse vs cannibal troglodytes. Slow, then horrific
br.warn: One of the most gruesome scenes in any film.

core.t: Once Upon a Time in the West
core.b: Leone's masterpiece: Henry Fonda as a villain, Claudia Cardinale, Bronson's harmonica. Slow and operatic.
core.w: Nearly three hours, and it takes its time.

beyond.b: Michael Cimino's three-and-a-half-hour folly that sank a studio. Beautiful, baggy and fascinating.
